title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
description:
On August 24, 79 AD, **Mount Vesuvius** erupted catastrophically, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under volcanic ash and pumice.

The eruption ejected a cloud of stones, ash, and volcanic gases to a height of 33 kilometers. An estimated 16,000 people died from the eruption, primarily from thermal shock and asphyxiation.

The buried cities were rediscovered in the 18th century, providing an extraordinary detailed insight into life in the Roman Empire.
